newsitem.title: CHILE: Whole hemisphere wants free trade pact-Chile's Frei.
newsitem.headline: Whole hemisphere wants free trade pact-Chile's Frei.

text.p: Chilean President Eduardo Frei said on Wednesday a proposed free trade zone covering all of the Americas was the aspiration of the whole hemisphere.

Frei, in his annual speech to Congress, said he hoped the Clinton administration would overcome its own domestic obstacles to creating the Free Trade Area of the Americas (FTAA), proposed by U.S. President Bill Clinton in 1994.

Frei said Chile, next in line to join the North American Free Trade Agreement since before Clinton took office, still hoped to reach a free trade agreement with the United States as a step toward the FTAA.
"During my visit to the United States in February, I reiterated our interest in reaching a trade agreement with that country, our main trading partner," said Frei in his 71-page speech.

"We think that such an agreement would contribute powerfully to the creation of a Free Trade Area of the Americas, the aspiration of the whole hemisphere," he said. "We hope that the internal obstacles faced by the United States government to initiate this negotiation can be overcome."

He seemed to be referring to opposition in the U.S. Congress to granting "fast-track" authority to U.S. negotiators. That authority is needed to begin full-scale talks for Chile to join NAFTA or for talks toward a continent-wide free trade deal.

Chilean officials have said in the past they support moving quickly toward the hemispheric trade deal, rather than strengthening the South American Mersocur bloc, which includes Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay. Chile has an "association agreement" with Mercosur but has said it is not interested in becoming a full member.
